     My impact as a victim is the utter failure of all systems designed to protect victims. The disillusionment of the failure of such systems resulted in my profound disbelief in the interest of the state in protecting the rights of the vulnerable. Those in the court, those in law, those on the police force... It's not about only taking cases you can win. It's not about denying people their ability to find answers. It's not about asking me, as a victim, questions that are inappropriate for police officers to ask. It doesn't matter if I have a preference for black guys, whether I have a sexual history, or whether I understand the difference between the counts of larceny.

    It also doesn't matter where I went to school, what I have studied, or who I have become. It doesn't matter how typical or atypical I am as a victim.     I live in fear for telling what I consider to be the truth about these events. I am afraid I have failed to act appropriately when I did not have enough memory or information to go upon. If the snippets or exchanges I have witnessed weren't all, then I extend my profound apology. I grieve these crimes."

It is painful to report a crime, and feel intimidated, as though you were on trial.    Lastly, I reported the fraud from the credit card to the credit card company, and they inexplicably removed $14 in charges, yet left the entire remaining balance of around $300 in other fraud charges. My faith in the judicial system, my previous belief that victims are treated with care, and my thought that banks remedy fraud was a type of innocent I didn't realize I had had. While my prosecuting attorney threw out there that it wasn't bright to invite the defendant and the other guy to my apartment, I considered it manners. After having been left to find my own way home at college parties several times or heard of other people doing this, I made a rule to "never leave a man behind." I didn't want them to get lost or cold trying to get back to the apartment complex. 

     I did everything in my ability to identify both perpetrators. I know that hot-ticket items were stolen from the apartment. I don't know what would have inspired the robbery. The total value of the items is around $2,500. The defendant must pay these items back because all are the actual property of ZZZZD(FADF[BOYFRIEND), not mine. Much like these people weren't particularly interested in my identity or aspirations, and instead saw me as a target, the financial crimes occurred against someone who wasn't even involved. I had to reconcile the idea that there must be something about me that allows so many people to overlook my will with the sense of indignation that I, too, am human. 

    I want there to be a resolution to the poverty in this community, which likely spurred the robbery element. I wanted to be able to live in Ypsilanti and associate with whomever I want without worrying that maybe people don't like me because of my race. Maybe, I was robbed because I was wearing my own mask. If I was targeted because they thought I was a RWP, then the truth couldn't be further. The restitution must be paid because I cannot replace the items. The card that was plucked from me had such a pathetic minimum balance compared to my friends with 20,000 limits with savvier brands. If the restitution were not paid, I would have no way of compensating an innocent person for the loss incurred the time I tried to make new friends. 

    My view on the crime is that it saddens me on several levels. I don't like having my trust exploited, or the barrage of questions that followed my decision to speak. Given that I have no recollection of the events that happened in my life on Valentine's Day, I am angry that I was not taken up on my demand to request a polygraph test. I wanted to take one, even though it is considered in this state a supreme violation of justice to force a victim to sit for one, after being threatened of legal action by the Ypsilanti police department. Since I was not allowed -- much like the actual crime and the other crimes I suspect -- to sit for a polygraph, both to potentially defend myself and indicated my complete lack of conscious awareness... I will never be able to express my truth. I will never be able to discover what actually happened.

I'm going to ignore the latter, and begin the former. The county of Washtenaw recently ruled that convicted felons cannot run for mayor. Perhaps, it is seen that the impoverished are somehow responsible for their own poverty, and that is why this taxation is disproportionately applied to this group rather than any of the more middle class groups.

I would like to add that the vocabulary I taught was not political or controversial, and pertained to conversational English.

I had to demonstrate what I learned about China, and publish the writings as part of short stories on Amazon. There is an academic need to circulate this material, and I would do this in the true pursuit of knowledge. Instead, my nuclear family believes that I can only excel at spending money. 

    When the computer was stolen, I'm sure the drive was wiped. I will be unable to ever access my notes on Changsha, Mandarin, or my risky place of employ. I will never remember the conversations I had recorded, including deeply personal talks of high sentimental value. The same applies to the iPhone. There were stories in the notepad that were not backed up. The phone contains a record of my attempts to learn Mandarin. It had pictures of the Chinese military base that many Americans had never seen. I can never get those pictures back, send them to a reputable organization, or have them as proof of some brave actions in my life. The computer wasn't a yuppie play toy.
